question: A researcher's chat approaches its context limit, and Claude begins condensing the earlier messages in that conversation. Which two statements about this are accurate? Select two.
options: A) Condensing raises the context window of that single chat right up to the next size that is available.
B) Condensing permanently erases those earlier messages from the conversation history for good.
C) Claude condenses the earlier messages so that the conversation is able to carry on past that point.
D) The full chat history remains accessible to her even after the earlier messages are condensed.
E) Condensing appears as a signal that her account has run out of usage allowance for the period.
correct_answers: C) Claude condenses the earlier messages so that the conversation is able to carry on past that point.
D) The full chat history remains accessible to her even after the earlier messages are condensed.
explanations: Incorrect. The window is a property of the model in use, and condensing does not enlarge it.
Incorrect. Nothing is erased, so treating condensing as deletion misreads what is happening in the conversation.
Correct. As a conversation nears the context limit, earlier messages are condensed so the chat can continue rather than stop.
Correct. Condensing changes what is held in working memory; the full history of the conversation stays available to read.
Incorrect. This confuses length limits with usage limits; nearing a context limit says nothing about the period's allowance.
